recap.text: Each squad leader receives twenty flags, Carl's a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers on a glowing spike, and one stabbed into a creature below five percent health turns it into a card. Carl carries Sister Ines's flag in his mouth and stabs it into a monk seal, then flags the dying Asojano and catches SlugPox. Sister Ines jabs a flag into Paz's neck so he cannot leave, and he becomes a card.

beats.headline: Twenty flags, one logo
beats.text: The floor's announcement ends with a gift: each squad leader receives a set of twenty flags carrying the squad's logo, created by the system itself. Plant one in the body of a living entity below five percent health and it becomes something called a T'Ghee totem in the squad leader's inventory. Carl's breath catches; he knows the word from the Cookbook. Noncorporeal monsters count too, and a flagged monster becomes a minion of whoever summons it, obedient to a point. Lose the flags before the squad is full and they are not replaced.
beats.gist: Donut's squad leader gets twenty logo flags that turn nearly dead monsters into T'Ghee totems.

beats.headline: Heart boxers on a stick
beats.text: The flag is a little bigger than Carl's hand, the kind given to children to wave at a parade, and it is a miniature pair of heart-covered boxers flying sideways as if from a clothesline. A motorcycle-club patch is embroidered top and bottom: The Royal Court of Princess Donut. An embroidered bomb patch sits over the crotch. It is tacky. Elle's squad got a bag of adult diapers and Imani's a butterfly, Donut reports, and why could they not get something like that? Its pole is a glowing metal spike about a foot long, enchanted to stick into any creature, ghosts too, below five percent health.
beats.gist: The flag is tacky heart-covered boxers on a spike that sticks into any creature below five percent health.

beats.headline: A flag in his mouth
beats.text: Sister Ines's squad lost a flag tying it to a crossbow bolt: it has to be physically touching whoever shoves it in. So she hands Carl one of hers, Team Sister Ines on a blue field around a black-and-white embroidered blob that may be a ball and chain wearing a nun's habit, almost as dumb as his own. Carl carries it in his mouth into the fight with the monk seal, gets an arm caught, takes the flag out and stabs it into the side of the seal's head. Pling. The seal is a card, and it belongs to Team Sister Ines.
beats.gist: Sister Ines's bolt-tied flag fails, so Carl carries her lent flag and stabs the seal, claiming it.

beats.headline: A flag in a god
beats.text: Carl comes to a decision. He pulls a flag and jumps at the dying Asojano just as his health starts to blink. The grass skirts are gone, and what is left is a pale, albino man, wide-eyed and afraid, half his face covered in festering boils. Carl shoves the flag into the top of his head, and Asojano puffs away into a card. A warning arrives: Carl has been infected with SlugPox. His momentum slams him into the wall.
beats.gist: Carl jams a flag into Asojano's head, turning him into a card, and catches SlugPox.

beats.headline: Into Paz's neck
beats.text: Paz has asked to be let go, and he says goodbye. Sister Ines will not have it: he is not leaving her, everyone leaves her. She suddenly has a flag in her hand and jabs it into his neck, so fast that it does not occur to Carl to try to stop her. Whoom. Paz is a card.
beats.gist: Sister Ines jabs a flag into Paz's neck, and he becomes a card.
